# Reduktion (phenomenological reduction) - chronological ledger

*Generated by `scripts/synthesis_ledger.py` from `synthesis/extractions/reduktion/`. Do not edit by hand - edit the extraction records and rebuild.*

*Core distinction: Husserl's phenomenological reduction as method (epoché, transcendental-methodical standpoint) versus Heidegger's destruction (Destruktion) as dismantling of philosophical tradition—both critical for phenomenological inquiry but different aims and procedures. Translation variants matter: 'epoché' vs 'bracketing' both appear in English commentaries. Watch for ambiguous uses of 'reduction' in mathematical or logical contexts; term carries significant density in Ideas I commentary and Cartesian Meditations. Bernet and Derrida commentaries are key secondary sources.*

240 units and 16 recorded absences from 29 commentaries.

### 1910-1911 - Husserl, Hua 13 — Basic Problems of Phenomenology

`husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary`

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua13/001` · *phenomenological reduction*

  > The *first* philosopher who carried out a phenomenological reduction — though he performed it only to surrender it again at once — was *Descartes*.

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua13/002` · *cogitatio, pure consciousness*
  What the empirical psychologist takes as psychic experience becomes cogitatio in the absolute sense only through the phenomenological reduction.
  `husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary#h3-s-16-descartes-fundamental-consideration-and-the-phenomenological-reduction` · Hua XIII § 16 · [§ 16\.   > first becomes *cogitatio in the absolute sense* — in the sense of *pure phenomenological givenness* — *through* the phenomenological reduction

- **criticized** · `reduktion/hua13/003` · *Cartesian fundamental consideration*
  Descartes' procedure failed because he attempted to ground absolute science without any systematic phenomenology of the field he had reached.
  `husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary#h3-s-16-descartes-fundamental-consideration-and-the-phenomenological-reduction` · Hua XIII § 16 · [§ 16\.   > Descartes reached the field of pure consciousness and immediately abandoned it, pressing on to prove God and the external world, precisely because he lacked the systematic discipline that would have shown what that field contains and demands.

  The objection is raised that a reduction wanting to switch off the own I is unthinkable, since the relation to the I is essential to the cogitatio.

  > the phenomenological reduction, which wants to switch off the own I, is something *unthinkable*

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua13/005` · *bracketing of the empirical I*
  Husserl grants the bracketing of the empirical I as indisputable and leaves the pure I open as a question for what the reduced attitude actually finds.
  `husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary#h3-s-19-the-objection-against-the-phenomenological-switch-off-ability-of-the-i` · Hua XIII § 19 · [§ 19\.   > phenomenological research can and must speak of *everything it finds* in its attitude

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua13/006` · *all-embracing phenomenological reduction*
  The all-embracing reduction switches off every existence-positing of natural givenness without doubting it, excluding in principle every empirically founded judgment as premise.
  `husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary#h3-s-32-repetition-and-new-presentation-the-phenomenological-reduction-to-the-pure` · Hua XIII § 32 · [§ 32\.   > we switch off *all* transcendence in the sense of natural existence-positing. We will make *no judgment-use* of any existence that comes to us as *natural* givenness — *without*, however, doubting it or suspecting it in any way.

  In this course the reduction does not coincide with a turn to essences but yields a world of individual being, the world of pure consciousness.
  `husserliana-13-basic-problems-of-phenomenology-commentary#h3-s-32-repetition-and-new-presentation-the-phenomenological-reduction-to-the-pure` · Hua XIII § 32 · [§ 32\. ### 1912 - Hua 5 - Ideas III

`husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary`

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua5/001` · *eidetic reduction*
  An eidetic reduction can be performed that excludes all questions of real existence and turns research to the eidos, for instance the essence perception.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h3-s8-rational-psychology-and-phenomenology-experimental-psychology` · Hua V § 8 · [§8.   > we can also perform an “eidetic reduction” — exclude all questions of real existence and carry out purely eidetic research

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua5/002` · *phenomenological reductions*
  Whoever cannot carry out the phenomenological reductions and grasp pure consciousness as idea is barred from entry into transcendental phenomenology and into philosophy in general.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h3-s12-further-clarification-of-the-relation-of-rational-psychology-and-phenomenolo` · Hua V § 12 · [§12.   > who cannot carry out the phenomenological reductions and grasp the pure, absolutely posited experience, the pure consciousness as idea — for him, entry into transcendental phenomenology and into philosophy in general is barred

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua5/003` · *reduction (and the absolute)*
  Only through reduction to pure consciousness is the absolute to be won, the absolute relatum for all realities, whose being is throughout relative.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h3-s12-further-clarification-of-the-relation-of-rational-psychology-and-phenomenolo` · Hua V § 12 · [§12.   > only through reduction to this is the “absolute” to be won, the absolute relatum for all realities, whose being is throughout relative being

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua5/004` · *reduction (eidetic and purifying from realization)*
  Every description of psychic experiences passes into a purely phenomenological one through an ideally possible reduction that is both eidetic and purifying from realization.
  `husserliana-5-ideas-iii-commentary#h3-s17-the-significance-of-ontological-concepts-for-psychology` · Hua V § 17 · [§17.   > every description of psychic experiences passes, through the ideally possible reduction (eidetic and purifying from realization), into a purely phenomenological one

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua5/005` · *phenomenological reduction*
  Transcendental experience becomes possible only through a radical change of the attitude in which natural worldly experience runs its course, a change called phenomenological reduction.

  > Transcendental experience becomes possible only through a radical change of the attitude in which natural, worldly experience runs its course — a change called “phenomenological reduction.”

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua5/006` · *phenomenological reduction (as attitude-change)*
  The attitude-change called the reduction is performed by the philosophizing person from the natural attitude in which one experiences oneself as a human person living among others in the world.

### 1913-1928 - Husserl, Hua 3 — Ideas I, Parts 3–4

`husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary`

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/001` · *phenomenological reductions*
  Observing the norms the reductions prescribe and switching off all transcendencies opens an all-sidedly infinite field of eidetic cognitions.
  `husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary#h3-s-63-the-particular-significance-of-methodological-considerations-for-phenomenol` · Ideas I § 63 · [§ 63\. The Particular Significance of Methodological Considerations for Phenomenology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary.html#the-particular-significance-of-methodological-considerations-for-phenomenology)
  > If we observe the norms that the phenomenological reductions prescribe to us, switch off all transcendencies exactly as they demand, take the experiences thus purely according to their own essence, then there opens to us

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/002` · *reduction as method-before-method*
  Phenomenology needs a method before any matter-determining method, one required merely to bring transcendentally-pure consciousness into the grasping gaze.
  `husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary#h3-s-63-the-particular-significance-of-methodological-considerations-for-phenomenol` · Ideas I § 63 · [§ 63\. The Particular Significance of Methodological Considerations for Phenomenology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary.html#the-particular-significance-of-methodological-considerations-for-phenomenology)
  > the reduction is a *method-before-method*, required just to bring pure consciousness into view

- **criticized** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/003` · *switching-off (Ausschaltung)*
  A self-referential objection is raised: if the reduction brackets the whole natural world, the phenomenologist as a member of that world appears to be bracketed along with it.
  `husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary#h3-s-64-the-self-switching-off-of-the-phenomenologist` · Ideas I § 64 · [§ 64\. The Self-Switching-Off of the Phenomenologist](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary.html#the-self-switching-off-of-the-phenomenologist)
  > But did we not just say "we" switch off — can we phenomenologists set ourselves out of play, we who are after all also members of the natural world?

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/004` · *norm of phenomenological reduction*
  The reduction is a methodical norm on what may be entered into phenomenology's results, forbidding any proposition containing natural positings.
  `husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary#h3-s-64-the-self-switching-off-of-the-phenomenologist` · Ideas I § 64 · [§ 64\. The Self-Switching-Off of the Phenomenologist](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary.html#the-self-switching-off-of-the-phenomenologist)
  > forbids us to enter any proposition that explicitly or implicitly contains such natural positings

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/005` · *self-switching-off*
  Self-switching-off excludes the phenomenologist's empirical existence from the eidetic content of his results rather than annihilating the performer of the reduction.
  `husserliana-3-ideas-i-parts-3-4-commentary#h3-s-64-the-self-switching-off-of-the-phenomenologist` · Ideas I § 64 · [§ 64\.   > The "self-switching-off" is thus the *exclusion of the phenomenologist's empirical existence from the eidetic content* of his results, *not* a paradoxical self-annihilation.

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/006` · *phenomenological reduction*
  Through the reduction transcendental consciousness results as the realm of absolute being, the primal region in which all other regions are rooted.

  > Through the phenomenological reduction, the realm of transcendental consciousness had resulted for us as the realm of "absolute" being in a determinate sense.

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/007` · *method of the phenomenological reduction*
  The distinction between being as consciousness and transcendent being can be won in its purity only through the method of the reduction.

  > And this distinction, Husserl notes, can be won and appreciated in its purity only through the method of the phenomenological reduction.

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua3-p34/008` · *switching-off as revaluing change of sign*
  Switching-off carries the character of a revaluing change of sign, so that what is bracketed re-enters the phenomenological sphere carrying an index.

  > a *becoming-free from the discipline for Dasein itself*, seizing the possibility of making Dasein the theme of a research determined by Dasein itself. This freeing is at once a freeing *from handed-down possibilities* of determining this being.

### 1923-1924 - Husserl, Hua 7 — Erste Philosophie I

`husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary`

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua7/001` · *not letting pre-givenness count*
  Transcendental research may in principle not let the being-pre-given of objects count, treating their being-there as a problem of constitution rather than a premise.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-tenth-lecture-the-cartesian-meditations` · [Tenth Lecture: The Cartesian Meditations](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#tenth-lecture-the-cartesian-meditations)
  > To "not let pre-givenness count" is the methodological refusal — the seed of the *epoché* — to take the being-there of objects as a premise rather than as itself a problem of constitution.

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua7/002` · *method of the phenomenological reduction*
  Pure inner experience requires a proper method, the method of the phenomenological reduction, in order to come about at all and to keep its purity scientifically secured.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-thirteenth-lecture-the-empiricist-prejudices-the-psychologism-in-the-theory-of-c` · [Thirteenth Lecture: The empiricist prejudices — the psychologism in the theory of cognition](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#thirteenth-lecture-the-empiricist-prejudices--the-psychologism-in-the-theory-of-cognition)
  > in order to come about at all, to obtain its purity, and to carry with itself scientific security of the preservation of this purity, *a proper method, the method of the phenomenological reduction*

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua7/003` · *phenomenological reduction (as remedy)*
  The reduction is named as the still-outstanding remedy for the historical failure of inner description, whose observers' findings never harmonized.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-thirteenth-lecture-the-empiricist-prejudices-the-psychologism-in-the-theory-of-c` · [Thirteenth Lecture: The empiricist prejudices — the psychologism in the theory of cognition](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#thirteenth-lecture-the-empiricist-prejudices--the-psychologism-in-the-theory-of-cognition)
  > having named the phenomenological reduction as the still-outstanding remedy

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua7/004` · *reduction of all cognition-problems to inner experience*
  Once Locke's confusion of sensation and reflection is clarified, his procedure is to be designated as the reduction of all cognition-problems to the ground of inner or consciousness-experience.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-fourteenth-lecture-the-exemplariness-of-modern-natural-science-as-a-hindering-mo` · [Fourteenth Lecture: The exemplariness of modern natural science as a hindering motive for the formation of a genuine intuitionistic science of consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#fourteenth-lecture-the-exemplariness-of-modern-natural-science-as-a-hindering-motive-for-the-formation-of-a-genuine-intuitionistic-science-of-consciousness)
  > the Lockean procedure is to be designated, in the right sense, as the *reduction of all cognition-problems to the ground of inner experience, of pure idea-experience or consciousness-experience*

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua7/005` · *phenomenological reduction (as universal ground)*
  After the methodical bringing-into-relief of the phenomenological reduction as the universal ground of research, the whole work is carried out within the phenomenological attitude itself.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-sixth-lecture-the-basic-features-of-the-positively-constructing-line-of-m` · Ideen I · [Twenty-sixth Lecture: The basic features of the positively constructing line of modern rationalism and its dogmatism](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-sixth-lecture-the-basic-features-of-the-positively-constructing-line-of-modern-rationalism-and-its-dogmatism)
  > Although, after the methodical bringing-into-relief of the universal ground of phenomenological research (the phenomenological reduction), this whole work carries itself out *within the phenomenological attitude itself*

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua7/006` · *universal epoché*
  The genuine method requires that all cognition be set up merely as phenomenon and that nothing be posited first but the absolutely evident transcendental subjectivity.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-o` · [Twenty-seventh Lecture: On metaphysics and theory of cognition. The significance of Leibniz's monadology and Kant's critique of reason](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-of-leibnizs-monadology-and-kants-critique-of-reason)
  > all cognition, beginning from the simple experience-cognition up to all science, must be treated as *epistemologically questionable*, and according to the sense of this questionability all and every cognition

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua7/007` · *epoché (methodical prescription)*
  Everything pre-given, the sense-world and the science determining it, may only be posited as experienced of the experiencing.
  `husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary#h3-twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-o` · [Twenty-seventh Lecture: On metaphysics and theory of cognition. The significance of Leibniz's monadology and Kant's critique of reason](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-7-erste-philosophie-i-commentary.html#twenty-seventh-lecture-on-metaphysics-and-theory-of-cognition-the-significance-of-leibnizs-monadology-and-kants-critique-of-reason)
  > everything pre-given however self-evidently — the sense-world and the science determining it — may *only* be posited as *experienced of the experiencing*

  > Unnoticed prejudices direct his meditations, so that, taken as a whole, they already lacked the power of conviction for his contemporaries.

`lacan-seminar-1-freuds-papers-on-technique-commentary`

#### Recorded absences

- **absent** · `lacan-seminar-1-freuds-papers-on-technique-commentary#h3-jean-hyppolite-die-verneinung`
  Expected because: This section ranks highest in the theme's density for the commentary, and Hyppolite's reading of Verneinung turns on a 'suspension' in which the repressed is taken up as thought — a use the theme's search terms match but which is not the phenomenological suspension of the natural thesis.
  The other hits in this section come from Freud's Destruktionstrieb, the destruction drive, which the theme's search term 'Destruktion' matches and which has nothing to do with Heidegger's destruction of the history of ontology.
  [Jean Hyppolite: Die Verneinung](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/lacan/lacan-seminar-1-freuds-papers-on-technique-commentary.html#jean-hyppolite-die-verneinung)

- **absent** · `lacan-seminar-1-freuds-papers-on-technique-commentary#h3-rosine-lefort`
  Expected because: The second densest section for the theme, and a case presentation in which the analyst's abstention from intervening might have been read in phenomenological terms; the hits are again ordinary uses of 'suspension' and no technical form of the reduction occurs.
  [Rosine Lefort](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/lacan/lacan-seminar-1-freuds-papers-on-technique-commentary.html#rosine-lefort)

*Partial pass: The whole file was searched for the theme's technical forms (phenomenological / transcendental / eidetic reduction, Reduktion, epoché, bracketing, putting out of play, transcendental ego / attitude / reflection / standpoint, zu den Sachen selbst) and none occurs anywhere in it; the two densest sections, 'Jean Hyppolite: Die Verneinung' and 'Rosine Lefort', were then read and are recorded as absences. The commentary was not read end to end, so this stays partial.*

## Reception layer

*Read alongside the spine, not on it. A commentator's date orders the reception, not the doctrine.*

### 1961 - Derrida, Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie

`derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary`

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/001` · *reduction of all facticity*
  Husserl's Proto-, Arche- and Ur- prefixes mark phenomenological originarity, which is reached only after the reduction of all facticity, as against the merely chronological 'first'.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > whereas *Proto-*, *Arche-*, *Ur-* refer to *phenomenological originarity* — that of sense, of foundation, of right, *after the reduction of all facticity*

- **criticized** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/002` · *reduction (of ready-made geometry)*
  The reduction of constituted geometry requires as its point of departure the very constituted result it neutralizes, so a factual history of geometry must already have taken place.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > There must always *already have been in fact* a history of geometry for the reduction to be able to operate; I must already have a naïve knowledge of geometry and *must not begin at the origin*.

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/003` · *reduction of empirical history*
  Kant and Husserl perform the reduction of empirical history identically, so their fundamental difference cannot be located in it.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > If the difference between Kant and Husserl is fundamental, it cannot lie in the *reduction of empirical history* — both perform it identically.

- **criticized** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/004` · *eidetic reduction*
  In Kant the eidetic reduction freeing geometrical essence from empirical reality is always already effected rather than performed by a subject.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > the *spontaneous eidetic reduction* that frees the geometrical essence from all empirical reality — from sensible figuration as much as from the geometer's psychological *vécu* — is for Kant *always already effected*

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/005` · *Ausschaltung (switching-off)*
  In Ideas I historical data fall under the exclusion as facts and not as norms, the sciences being bracketed as cultural fact rather than as standard of validity.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · Ideas I §1, §56 · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > historical "data" are bracketed *as facts and not as norms*: in suspending the natural world one excludes all individual objectivities constituted by the axiological and practical functions of consciousness

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/006` · *first reductions of factual history*
  The reduction of factual history must precede any thematizing of the ideal object's own historicity, and those first reductions are never lifted.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > That is why these first reductions of factual history will *never be lifted*

- **criticized** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/007` · *eidetic and transcendental reductions*
  The account of geometry's genesis raises the expectation that the eidetic and transcendental reductions will simply be lifted in favour of a constituting history in which the founding fact is irreplaceable.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · O., 175-7 · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > one might expect him *purely and simply to lift* the eidetic and transcendental reductions and to return to a *constituting history* in which taking the fact into consideration *as such* would become indispensable

- **criticized** · `reduktion/derrida-geometrie/008` · *Husserlian reduction*
  Against Tran-Duc-Thao, the reduction never meant a negation or forgetting that quits the real conditions of sense and facticity, since sense is nothing other than the sense of reality or facticity.
  `derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary#h2-ii` · Tran-Duc-Thao, Phénoménologie et matérialisme dialectique, 1951 · [II](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-introduction-a-lorigine-de-la-geometrie-commentary.html#ii)
  > although the reduction never had the sense — quite the contrary — of a negation, an ignorance, or a forgetting that "quits" the real conditions of sense and facticity in general

*Partial pass: Covers section II (lines 57-140), which carries the commentary's sustained treatment of the reduction of empirical history, the Kant comparison, and the Tran-Duc-Thao dispute. Sections V, VII, IX, X and XI, which also carry hits, are not covered.*

`henry-philosophie-et-phenomenologie-du-corps-commentary`

- **revised** · `reduktion/henry-corps/006` · *deduction as reduction*

### 1967 - La voix et le phénomène

`derrida-la-voix-et-le-phenomene-commentary`

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/vp/001` · *the reductions (eidetic and phenomenological)*

- **criticized** · `reduktion/vp/002` · *bracketing of metaphysics*

  `derrida-la-voix-et-le-phenomene-commentary#h3-derrida-s-guiding-question` · VP pp. 1-16 · [Derrida’s Guiding Question](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-la-voix-et-le-phenomene-commentary.html#derridas-guiding-question)

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/vp/005` · *parallelism (Parallelität)*
  A radical difference that distinguishes nothing in fact separates phenomenological psychology from transcendental phenomenology, and in it alone resides the possibility of a transcendental question.
  `derrida-la-voix-et-le-phenomene-commentary#h3-the-parallels-phenomenological-psychology-and-transcendental-phenomenology` · VP pp. 1-16 · [The Parallels: Phenomenological Psychology and Transcendental Phenomenology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/derrida/derrida-la-voix-et-le-phenomene-commentary.html#the-parallels-phenomenological-psychology-and-transcendental-phenomenology)

- **revised** · `reduktion/vp/008` · *reduction*

### 1981 - Franck, Chair et corps

`franck-chair-et-corps-commentary`

- **revised** · `reduktion/franck-chair/001` · *phenomenological reduction*
  The reduction is distinguished from Cartesian doubt: it neither negates nor doubts, it is definitive and universal, and it encompasses the psyche that Descartes leaves intact.

  The reduction is the pivot and permanent theme of Husserl's enterprise, the pure origin of all meaning and what opens the phenomenological domain.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-two-science-as-egology` · [Chapter Two: Science as Egology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-two-science-as-egology)

  Husserl warns that what the reductions produce as transcendentally absolute is not what is ultimate, but constitutes itself from a primal source that is truly absolute.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity` · Ideas I · [Chapter Five: Eidetic Reduction and Archi-Facticity](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity)
  > the transcendentally "absolute" that the reductions have produced is not really what is ultimate; it is something that constitutes itself in a profound and completely peculiar sense of its own, with its primal source in what is ultimately and truly absolute

- **introduced** · `reduktion/franck-chair/008` · *eidetic analysis*
  The charge that transcendental analysis merely transfers the empirical de facto ego onto the transcendental is met only by the transcendental analysis becoming eidetic.
  `franck-chair-et-corps-commentary#h2-chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity` · [Chapter Five: Eidetic Reduction and Archi-Facticity](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-chair-et-corps-commentary.html#chapter-five-eidetic-reduction-and-archi-facticity)
  > Indeed — this would be the case if the transcendental analysis did not become an *eidetic* analysis.

*Partial pass: Covers Chapter Two, 'Science as Egology', and Chapter Five, 'Eidetic Reduction and Archi-Facticity'. Chapters Six, Eight and Nine also carry hits and are not covered.*

### 1986 - Franck, Heidegger and the Problem of Space

`franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary`

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/franck-space/001` · *phenomenological destruction of the tradition*

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/franck-space/002` · *reduction of consciousness*
  The relation of being to the essence of the human being is inaccessible without a displacement and reduction of consciousness, since from consciousness things cannot be reached in their worldliness.
  `franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary#h1-chapter-i-the-question-of-being` · [Chapter I — The Question of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary.html#chapter-i--the-question-of-being)

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/franck-space/003` · *reduction (Husserlian parallel)*
  As transcendental subjectivity covered over by the psyche surges forth in its own being thanks to the reduction, so Dasein initially understands itself from out of the world of things.
  `franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary#h1-chapter-i-the-question-of-being` · [Chapter I — The Question of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary.html#chapter-i--the-question-of-being)

- **introduced** · `reduktion/franck-space/004` · *phenomenological reduction*
  The phenomenological reduction is defined as the leading-back of the inquiring gaze from naively grasped beings toward being.
  `franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary#h1-chapter-i-the-question-of-being` · [Chapter I — The Question of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary.html#chapter-i--the-question-of-being)
  > the fundamental component of the phenomenological method, in the sense of the *leading-back of the inquiring gaze from naively grasped beings toward being*, is what is designated *phenomenological reduction*

- **revised** · `reduktion/franck-space/005` · *transcendental reduction (contrast)*
  This reduction shares with Husserl's transcendental reduction only the purely formal trait of a conversion of the gaze, and nothing of its content.
  `franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary#h1-chapter-i-the-question-of-being` · [Chapter I — The Question of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary.html#chapter-i--the-question-of-being)
  > this reduction shares with Husserl's *transcendental* reduction *only the purely formal trait* of a *conversion of the gaze* — and nothing of its content

- **introduced** · `reduktion/franck-space/006` · *phenomenological construction*
  The second component is phenomenological construction, the projection of the pre-given being with regard to its being and ontological structures.
  `franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary#h1-chapter-i-the-question-of-being` · [Chapter I — The Question of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary.html#chapter-i--the-question-of-being)
  > The *projection of the pre-given being*, with regard to its being and its ontological structures, is what is called *phenomenological construction*.

- **introduced** · `reduktion/franck-space/007` · *destruction*
  The third component is destruction, required because the history of ontology covers over the possibility of fundamental-ontological construction as a forgetting of the first experiences of being.
  `franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary#h1-chapter-i-the-question-of-being` · [Chapter I — The Question of Being](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/fanck/franck-heidegger-and-the-problem-of-space-commentary.html#chapter-i--the-question-of-being)
  > The history of ontology *covers over* the possibility of fundamental-ontological construction; it constitutes a *forgetting of the first experiences of being* that lie at the origin of metaphysics.

*Partial pass: Covers the Introduction and Chapter I, 'The Question of Being'. The later chapters on space are not covered.*

The First Word on the Being of Beings: cogitatio](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-first-word-on-the-being-of-beings-cogitatio)

The Second Word on the Being of Beings: causa](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-second-word-on-the-being-of-beings-causa)

### 1994 - Rudolf Bernet, La vie du sujet: Recherches sur l'interprétation de Husserl dans la phénoménologie — Commentary

`bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary`

- **introduced** · `reduktion/bernet/001` · *reduction (Rückführung)*
  The reduction is agreed across the current French debate to be a leading-back of philosophical thought to phenomena that the reduction itself first makes appear.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h2-introduction-the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subject-s-double-life` · La vie du sujet, pp. 5-6 · [Introduction — The Phenomenological Reduction and the Subject's Double Life](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#introduction--the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subjects-double-life)
  > Everyone treats the reduction as a leading-back (*Rückführung*) of philosophical thought to phenomena; but the phenomena in question are those whose appearing requires the reduction itself

- **revised** · `reduktion/bernet/002` · *reduction*
  Bernet places the scission the reduction opens inside the phenomenological phenomenon itself rather than between phenomenological and ordinary phenomena.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h2-introduction-the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subject-s-double-life` · La vie du sujet, pp. 7-8 · [Introduction — The Phenomenological Reduction and the Subject's Double Life](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#introduction--the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subjects-double-life)
  > The scission the reduction introduces thus falls not between rational phenomenological phenomena and irrational ordinary ones but within the phenomenological phenomenon itself

- **introduced** · `reduktion/bernet/003` · *impartial spectator*
  Husserl distinguishes the world-constituting subject, which the reduction exhibits, from the impartial spectator, which performs the reduction.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h2-introduction-the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subject-s-double-life` · La vie du sujet, pp. 8-9 · [Introduction — The Phenomenological Reduction and the Subject's Double Life](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#introduction--the-phenomenological-reduction-and-the-subjects-double-life)
  > the first is what the reduction gives to be seen, the second is the agent who performs it

- **introduced** · `reduktion/bernet/004` · *Husserlian reduction*
  Fink's text presents the ontological import of the Husserlian reduction as making the difference between the being of the world and the pre-being of transcendental consciousness appear.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h3-husserl` · La vie du sujet, p. 10; Fink, Sixth Cartesian Meditation · [Husserl](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#husserl)
  > which is meant to make appear the difference between the "being" of the world and the "pre-being" (*Vor-Sein*) of transcendental consciousness

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/bernet/005` · *reduction (motivation of)*
  The Sixth Meditation finds no motive within natural life capable of compelling the change of life the reduction requires.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · La vie du sujet, pp. 11-12 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > No difficulty met with in natural life, no desire for clarification, no will to do scientific work has the power to extract a human being from immersion in the natural life accomplished within the world.

- **criticized** · `reduktion/bernet/006` · *reduction as reflection*
  The passage from the natural to the phenomenological phenomenon is not a reflective doubling of consciousness but a scission, and neither the subject-object nor the higher-order-consciousness model of reflection applies.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · La vie du sujet, pp. 12-13 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > It neither sets the constituting subject before the gaze by separating it from the constituted object, nor makes constituting consciousness the object of a second constituting consciousness.

- **revised** · `reduktion/bernet/007` · *reduction (ontological aim)*
  What the spectator first makes appear is the ontological difference between constituting consciousness and constituted world, so the reduction's aim is ontological.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness` · La vie du sujet, p. 13 · [The Being of the World and the Being of Constituting Consciousness](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-the-world-and-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness)
  > What appears for the first time thanks to the spectator is the ontological difference between constituting consciousness and constituted world

- **introduced** · `reduktion/bernet/008` · *Spaltung (split), universal epoché*
  The split of the transcendental subject follows directly from the reduction: in the universal epoché the spectator produces itself by separating from constituting consciousness.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-sp` · La vie du sujet, pp. 14-15 · [The Being of Constituting Consciousness and the Being of the Phenomenological Spectator](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-spectator)
  > The split (*Spaltung*) of the transcendental subject follows directly from the reduction: in the universal epoché the phenomenological spectator produces itself, separating itself from constituting consciousness in order to make the latter appear as its counterpart.

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/bernet/009` · *phenomenological spectator*
  The spectator, unlike constituting consciousness, has no anonymous pre-reductive existence in natural life.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-sp` · La vie du sujet, pp. 14-15 · [The Being of Constituting Consciousness and the Being of the Phenomenological Spectator](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-spectator)
  > There is, by contrast, no phenomenological spectator that would be ignorant of itself while working anonymously in natural life — the spectator does not exist before the reduction.

- **criticized** · `reduktion/bernet/010` · *Unbeteiligtheit (non-participation) of the spectator*
  Husserl corrects Fink's account of the spectator's worldlessness by redescribing its disinterest as a different interest, in the world's origin in transcendental consciousness.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h4-the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-sp` · La vie du sujet, p. 16 · [The Being of Constituting Consciousness and the Being of the Phenomenological Spectator](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#the-being-of-constituting-consciousness-and-the-being-of-the-phenomenological-spectator)
  > Husserl's correction is the more accurate formulation: the spectator is interested in the origin of the world in transcendental consciousness, rather than uninterested in the world.

- **revised** · `reduktion/bernet/011` · *phenomenological reduction (Heidegger's formulation)*
  Heidegger keeps the reduction as a fundamental piece of phenomenological method while redirecting it from transcendental consciousness to the understanding of the being of a being.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h3-heidegger` · La vie du sujet, pp. 18-19; Heidegger 1927 course · [Heidegger](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#heidegger)
  > For Heidegger, it leads the gaze back from any grasp whatever of a being to the understanding of the being of that being, projected upon the mode of its unconcealment (*Unverborgenheit*).

- **revised** · `reduktion/bernet/012` · *second reduction (anxiety, call of conscience)*
  Anxiety performs in Heidegger what the reduction performs in Husserl and Fink, bringing Dasein before a new self and before the phenomenon of its own being.
  `bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary#h3-heidegger` · La vie du sujet, pp. 20-21 · [Heidegger](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/bernet/bernet-la-vie-du-sujet-commentary.html#heidegger)
  > Like the reduction in Husserl and Fink, anxiety brings it about that Dasein, finding itself face to face and alone with itself, encounters for the first time not only a new self but the phenomenon of its own being.

*Partial pass: Covers the Introduction, 'The Phenomenological Reduction and the Subject's Double Life', through its Husserl half and the 'Heidegger' section (lines 23-88): the framing of the reduction, the Fink Sixth Cartesian Meditation material, and the comparison with Heidegger. The two Heidegger subsections that follow and the later chapters are not covered.*

### undated - Commentary on Husserl, Zur Phänomenologie der Intersubjektivität, Erster Teil: 1905–1920 (Husserliana XIII)

`husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary`

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/001` · *phenomenological reduction*
  Kern dates the working-out of the idea of the phenomenological reduction as the most fundamental of all methods to the years 1905 to 1909.
  `husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary#h2-editor-s-introduction-iso-kern` · Hua XIII, Einleitung des Herausgebers, XXIV-XXV · [Editor's Introduction (Iso Kern)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary.html#editors-introduction-iso-kern)
  > 1905 to 1909, the years in which he worked out the idea of phenomenological reduction as the most fundamental of all methods

- **presupposed** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/002` · *phenomenological reduction (first occurrence)*
  By Husserl's own judgement the concept and correct use of the phenomenological reduction are first found in the manuscript complex of summer 1905, and the method was developed in the courses of 1906/07 and 1907.
  `husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary#h2-editor-s-introduction-iso-kern` · [Editor's Introduction (Iso Kern)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary.html#editors-introduction-iso-kern)
  > By Husserl's own judgement the concept and the correct use of "phenomenological reduction" are first found in the manuscript complex

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/003` · *reduction (and intersubjectivity)*
  The position of the reduction forced Husserl into the problem of how a plurality of mutually separate absolute consciousnesses can be reached on a method that goes back to pure and absolute consciousness.
  `husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary#h2-editor-s-introduction-iso-kern` · [Editor's Introduction (Iso Kern)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary.html#editors-introduction-iso-kern)
  > how, on a method that goes back to pure and absolute consciousness, can a plurality and mutual separateness of absolute consciousnesses be reached and grounded?

- **criticized** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/004` · *reduction (its solipsistic reading)*
  The picture on which the reduction first isolates a solipsistic sphere that intersubjectivity is later called in to repair is inverted by the documents.
  `husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary#h2-editor-s-introduction-iso-kern` · [Editor's Introduction (Iso Kern)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary.html#editors-introduction-iso-kern)
  > The point deserves emphasis because it inverts a common picture: the reduction did not first isolate a solipsistic sphere that intersubjectivity was later called in to repair

- **revised** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/005` · *universal intersubjective reduction*
  Husserl refers to the 1910/11 course by working titles naming the extension of the reduction to empathy and to a universal intersubjective reduction.
  `husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary#h2-editor-s-introduction-iso-kern` · Hua XIII, Einleitung des Herausgebers, XXXV-XXXVI · [Editor's Introduction (Iso Kern)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary.html#editors-introduction-iso-kern)
  > "lecture on empathy and extended reduction," "lecture on phenomenological reduction as universal intersubjective reduction,"

- **criticized** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/006` · *phenomenological reduction (Husserl's retrospect)*
  Husserl confesses that his first cognition of the phenomenological reduction was restricted and that for years he saw no possibility of shaping it intersubjectively.
  `husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary#h2-editor-s-introduction-iso-kern` · Erste Philosophie, 1923/24 · [Editor's Introduction (Iso Kern)](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/husserl/husserliana-13-editors-introduction-commentary.html#editors-introduction-iso-kern)
  > for Husserl himself, as he confesses, the first cognition of phenomenological reduction was a restricted one; for years he saw no possibility of shaping it intersubjectively

- **introduced** · `reduktion/hua13-intro/007` · *double reduction of re-presentation*
  The achievement consists above all in the double reduction of re-presentation, in which the re-presented experiences contained in a re-presenting act are also grasped as phenomenologically pure consciousness.
